hints.title: Reverse Array Perspective
hints.text: Traversing backwards from right to left maintains cost bounds as suffixes naturally enforce non-decreasing ordering.

hints.title: Monotonic Deque Aggregation
hints.text: Store (value, count) pairs in a monotonic decreasing deque, merging smaller blocks and updating cumulative operation cost.

hints.title: Right Pointer Contraction
hints.text: Shrink right boundary j whenever operation cost exceeds k, then add j - i + 1 valid subarrays.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import deque

class Solution:
    def countNonDecreasingSubarrays(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        ans = 0
        cost = 0
        dq = deque()
        j = len(nums) - 1
        
        for i in range(len(nums) - 1, -1, -1):
            num = nums[i]
            count = 1
            while dq and dq[-1][0] < num:
                nxt_num, nxt_count = dq.pop()
                count += nxt_count
                cost += (num - nxt_num) * nxt_count
            dq.append((num, count))
            
            while cost > k:
                rm_num, rm_count = dq.popleft()
                cost -= (rm_num - nums[j])
                j -= 1
                if rm_count > 1:
                    dq.appendleft((rm_num, rm_count - 1))
                    
            ans += j - i + 1
            
        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Each element is inserted and evicted from monotonic deque at most once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating each subarray independently takes O(n^2) or O(n^3) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) deque stores compacted values and counts.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Applies monotonic deque with sliding window to dynamically maintain deficit cost in linear time.
